name: Personal Current Account Opening — Non-Functional Requirements
description: Per-phase NFRs for JRN-001. Defines latency targets, throughput (peak applications/hour), availability targets, security classification, data classification, and regulatory SLAs. NFRs reflect the operational reality of a UK mid-tier commercial bank (2–5 million retail customers), the Important Business Service obligations under PRA SS1/21 / FCA PS21/3, and the specific regulatory SLAs imposed by MLR 2017, CASS rules, and OFSI sanctions obligations.

baseline_assumptions.peak_hour_volume: A mid-tier UK bank processing c. 500 account applications per hour at peak (e.g., post-campaign launch, Monday morning). Sustained throughput model: 200 applications/hour average; 800 applications/hour peak for a major marketing campaign. Weekend peaks lower (c. 150/hour).
baseline_assumptions.important_business_service: Account Opening is classified as an Important Business Service (IBS) under PRA SS1/21. The bank must set and meet an impact tolerance for maximum tolerable disruption. Assumed impact tolerance: maximum 4 hours cumulative downtime in any 12-month rolling period for the full account opening journey.
baseline_assumptions.data_residency: All personal data (PII) and account data must remain within the UK. No PII traversal through non-UK CDN nodes or cloud regions.
baseline_assumptions.regulatory_reporting_reference: NFR SLAs for sanctions screening (PH-003) and OFSI notification (EX-002) are hard regulatory obligations, not performance aspirations. Non-compliance carries OFSI/FCA enforcement exposure.

latency.notes: Form rendering and submission via SVC-017 (Digital Channels). Preliminary eligibility check (age, residency, deduplication) must return within 800ms at p95. Sub-second form response is the baseline UX expectation set by neobank competitors (Monzo, Starling). Higher latency at p99 accommodates degraded network conditions on mobile (3G/4G).

throughput.burst_handling: Horizontal auto-scaling of SVC-017 and SVC-101 (API Gateway). Queue-backed processing — form submissions enqueued; eligibility check processed asynchronously if >200ms latency detected.
throughput.notes: CH-002 (Mobile App) drives ~70% of volume. Load testing must validate 800 concurrent application initiations without latency degradation above p95 thresholds.

availability.degraded_mode: If SVC-017 is partially degraded, static form capture with async submission is acceptable. Eligibility check may be deferred to PH-003 if deduplication service is unavailable, with compensating control at PH-003.
availability.planned_maintenance_window: 02:00–04:00 UTC Sundays (lowest traffic window). Application volume drops to <5/hour. BCOBS requires 24-hour advance notice to customers of any planned outage affecting account services.

nfr.security_notes: No authentication required at form initiation. Device fingerprinting and basic fraud signals (IP reputation, VPN/Tor detection, velocity check) are captured passively at this phase without customer visibility. CAPTCHA or proof-of-work challenge may be applied if bot-like submission patterns are detected. No PII stored until form submission — form data held client-side only until explicit submission.

data_classification.sensitivity: HIGH — UK GDPR personal data. Collected under Article 6(1)(b) (contract performance) and Article 6(1)(c) (legal obligation — MLR 2017 CDD). A DPIA is required for the automated processing of this data in subsequent phases.
data_classification.retention: Application data retained for 5 years post-application (completed or abandoned) per MLR 2017 record-keeping requirements and FCA Consumer Duty evidence obligations. Abandoned applications (no submission) purged after 48 hours.

regulatory_sla.obligation: No specific regulatory SLA for this phase. Consumer Duty (PS22/9) consumer understanding outcome requires the application flow to be clear and not misleading — no implied SLA but clarity standard applies to all screen content.
references: UK GDPR Article 6 (lawful basis for data collection)

latency.notes: Biometric + document verification via Onfido/Jumio is an external vendor API call. Vendor SLA is typically 2–5 seconds for automated decisions. The p95 target of 8 seconds accommodates document image upload time on mobile and vendor processing latency. Customers are shown a 'verifying...' state during this period — UX research indicates up to 10 seconds is acceptable before customers abandon. Liveness check adds ~2–3 seconds on top of document check.

throughput.burst_handling: Identity verification vendor (Onfido/Jumio) SLA must contractually guarantee capacity for peak throughput. Retry queue for failed vendor calls — maximum 3 automated retries with exponential backoff before manual fallback. Vendor capacity validation is a procurement contract obligation.
throughput.notes: Branch fallback (eKYC in branch) has a separate throughput model — branch appointments are booked individually; branch verification capacity is ~5–10 customers/hour per branch, handled offline from the digital path.

availability.degraded_mode: If identity verification vendor is unavailable, new digital identity verifications are queued for up to 2 hours. Beyond 2 hours, customers are proactively offered branch appointments. SCV-050 must implement vendor circuit-breaker and timeout to prevent cascading failures.
availability.dependency_sla: Onfido/Jumio vendor SLA must be contractually specified at 99.9% or above. Material outsourcing framework (PRA SS2/21) requires the bank to maintain a documented exit plan for the identity verification vendor.

nfr.security_notes: Document and biometric data is sensitive personal data under UK GDPR Article 9. Transmission to SVC-050 and the identity verification vendor must be over TLS 1.3 minimum. Biometric templates must never be stored by the bank — only the verification outcome (PASS/FAIL + confidence score) is retained. Document images are retained for CDD audit purposes for 5 years (MLR 2017 Regulation 40) but stored in encrypted, access-controlled storage (SVC-111). Vendor data processing agreement (DPA) under UK GDPR must be in place with Onfido/Jumio.

data_classification.sensitivity: HIGHEST — biometric data is Special Category data under UK GDPR Article 9. Requires explicit consent and DPIA. Document images are sensitive identity data requiring access controls and audit logging on every access event.
data_classification.retention: Identity verification outcome retained for 5 years (MLR 2017 Regulation 40 CDD record-keeping). Document images retained for 5 years in encrypted cold storage. Biometric template not retained — only liveness check outcome retained.
data_classification.data_residency: UK only. Document images must not traverse non-UK cloud regions. Vendor processing agreement must confirm UK/EEA data residency or an approved transfer mechanism under UK GDPR Article 46.

regulatory_sla.obligation: MLR 2017 Regulation 27 requires CDD to be completed before a business relationship is established. The identity verification phase is the first component of CDD. There is no prescribed time limit for completion, but the bank must not open an account until CDD is complete. The bank must be able to produce identity verification records for CDD audit within 2 business days of an FCA/NCA request.
references: UK GDPR Article 9 (special category biometric data)
PRA SS2/21 (material outsourcing — identity verification vendor)

latency.notes: PEP/sanctions screening (SVC-051) must return within 3,000ms in all conditions — this is a hard limit driven by the OFSI real-time screening obligation (GOV-005-R02). Batch-end or delayed screening is not compliant with OFSI expectations following the Starling Bank FCA enforcement action (October 2024, £29m fine for incomplete screening). Adverse media screening may run asynchronously (up to 5s) without blocking the sanctions result. Risk scoring is a local computation (sub-100ms) once screening results are available.

throughput.burst_handling: SVC-051 (Sanctions Screening) must be independently scalable. Peak campaign load must be load-tested against ComplyAdvantage/Refinitiv API capacity. Rate limit contracts with screening data vendors must cover peak throughput. Degraded mode: if vendor API latency exceeds 3,000ms, application is queued for up to 30 minutes before customer is notified of delay — no account may be provisioned until a CLEAR sanctions result is obtained.
throughput.notes: 100% coverage of all applicants is mandatory — no sampling or batching of sanctions screening. This is a direct FCA enforcement requirement (Starling Bank precedent). Throughput capacity must be proven by load test, not assumed.

availability.degraded_mode: No degraded mode for sanctions screening — the bank cannot open accounts during a complete sanctions screening outage. OFSI and FCA expect zero tolerance for unscreened accounts. Circuit-breaker must halt account openings, not skip screening. Vendor availability SLA must be contractually higher than 99.9%.
availability.dependency_sla: ComplyAdvantage/Refinitiv World-Check API: contractual SLA 99.95% uptime. Dual-vendor capability recommended for redundancy (primary + fallback screening vendor) given the no-degraded-mode constraint.

nfr.security_notes: Screening queries are made from SVC-051 to vendor APIs using service-account credentials (not customer credentials). Screening results contain sensitive PEP and sanctions match data — must be encrypted at rest and accessible only to compliance team (PER-052) and the onboarding orchestration service (SVC-050). All screening hits, including cleared hits, must be retained for a minimum of 5 years (GOV-005-R02). Audit log of every screening call, result, and downstream action must be immutably stored in SVC-111.

data_classification.sensitivity: HIGH — screening results may reveal PEP status or sanctions designation, which is sensitive regulatory data. Risk tier assignment is personal data under UK GDPR. Tipping-off prohibition (POCA 2002 s333A) means SAR-related flags must be access-controlled and not visible to non-compliance staff.
data_classification.retention: Screening records retained for 5 years (MLR 2017 Regulation 40). Risk tier records retained for duration of customer relationship plus 5 years for pKYC purposes.

regulatory_sla.obligation: Sanctions screening must be real-time (not batch) per OFSI obligation. A confirmed sanctions hit must be escalated to the MLRO immediately and OFSI notified within 14 days of confirmation. SAR submission to NCA UKFIU: within 5 business days of the MLRO forming a suspicion. CDD must be completed before account is established (MLR 2017 Regulation 27).
regulatory_sla.sanctions_notification_sla: 14 calendar days from confirmed OFSI designated person identification to OFSI notification
regulatory_sla.sar_submission_sla: 5 business days from MLRO forming a suspicion to NCA UKFIU submission

latency.notes: Automated decision engine (eligibility + KYC outcome combination) is a deterministic rule execution — no external API calls in the automated path. Sub-second at p50 is achievable. p95 accommodates minor latency from SVC-001 eligibility query and ApplicationDecisionMade event publication to event bus. Manual referral path (AP-001) does not have a machine latency — it enters a human review queue with a 3-business-day SLA.

throughput.burst_handling: Decision engine is stateless and horizontally scalable. Manual review queue capacity must be sized for peak referral volume — estimated 5–10% of applications referred in normal conditions; higher during regulatory change periods.
throughput.notes: Decision audit trail writes to SVC-103 (Audit & Logging) and SVC-111 (WORM store) for every decision. Write throughput of SVC-111 must be validated at peak application throughput.

availability.degraded_mode: If decision engine is unavailable, applications are queued with a customer-facing message ('Your application is being processed'). Applications are not abandoned. Maximum queue hold: 2 hours before customer notification. Decision engine unavailability does not trigger account opening without decision.

nfr.security_notes: Decision engine inputs (KYC result, identity outcome) and outputs (decision, decision basis) must be immutably logged. Decision audit trail must be tamper-evident (WORM-stored) as it is key evidence for FCA Consumer Duty supervision and potential FOS complaint adjudication. AI/ML models used in eligibility decisions must be documented and validated per PRA model risk management standards (PRA SS1/23).

data_classification.sensitivity: HIGH — decline decisions are sensitive data that may be subject to UK GDPR data subject access requests. Decision basis must be retained but may be subject to legal privilege exemptions where SAR-related.
data_classification.retention: Decision records retained for 5 years (FCA Consumer Duty evidence; MLR 2017 record-keeping). Decline decision audit trail retained for minimum 6 years to cover FOS complaint limitation period.

regulatory_sla.obligation: No statutory time limit on account decision, but Consumer Duty (PS22/9) consumer understanding outcome requires a timely decision communicated clearly. Manual referral (EDD) cases: 3-business-day target SLA (bank policy; consistent with MLR 2017 CDD 'reasonable time' standard). FOS complaint right: customers must be informed of their right to complain to FOS if dissatisfied with a decline, within the decline communication.
regulatory_sla.manual_referral_sla: 3 business days from KYCReferralRaised to ApplicationDecisionMade (MLRO sign-off for PEP cases)
references: FCA BCOBS (Banking Conduct of Business — fair treatment of applicants)

latency.notes: Account provisioning involves: SVC-001 ledger record creation, sort code/account number allocation, FSCS SCV update, CASS registration initiation, and CardIssuanceTriggered event publication. The Retail Banking Core (SVC-001) write is the critical path. SCV update must complete synchronously — the account is not considered fully provisioned until SCV is updated (FSCS compliance). CASS registration with Pay.UK is asynchronous and does not block the customer-facing provisioning confirmation.

throughput.burst_handling: SVC-001 write throughput must be load-tested to 800 account creations/hour. Sort code/account number allocation pool must have sufficient headroom (bank maintains an allocated block from Vocalink/Pay.UK — pool monitoring alerting when <10% capacity remains).
throughput.notes: Card issuance trigger (CardIssuanceTriggered event) dispatched to card processor (Marqeta/Thredd) asynchronously. Card processor throughput is not a bottleneck for account provisioning — card production is a downstream batch process.

availability.degraded_mode: If SVC-001 write fails, account opening is blocked (cannot provision without a ledger record). Applications are queued for up to 4 business hours before customer notification. Retry mechanism with idempotency keys prevents duplicate account creation. If SCV update fails, FSCS compliance alert is raised to IT Operations (PER-060) and Finance — no card issuance until SCV is consistent.
availability.ibs_note: Account Provisioning is part of the Important Business Service. PRA SS1/21 impact tolerance: maximum 4 hours cumulative disruption in a 12-month rolling period.

nfr.security_notes: SVC-001 account creation writes carry the highest data sensitivity in this journey — they create the financial record of ownership. All writes must be: (1) idempotent (idempotency key from application_ref to prevent duplicate accounts); (2) transactionally consistent (account record + SCV update must be atomic); (3) immutably audit-logged to SVC-111. Access to account creation APIs in SVC-001 is restricted to SVC-050 (Customer Onboarding Service) via mutual TLS service-to-service authentication.

data_classification.sensitivity: HIGHEST — this phase creates the authoritative financial account record. UK GDPR processing activity record (ROPA) must document the legal basis (Article 6(1)(b) contract) for storing this data indefinitely while the account relationship exists.
data_classification.retention: Account records retained for duration of account relationship plus 7 years (FCA BCOBS record-keeping; MLR 2017 post-relationship record-keeping). SCV retained for FSCS obligations.
data_classification.data_residency: UK only. Ledger data must be stored in UK-domiciled infrastructure only.

regulatory_sla.obligation: FSCS SCV: Single Customer View must be maintainable such that eligible deposit data can be extracted within 24 hours of a FSCS payout trigger. This requires SCV to be updated as part of account provisioning (not deferred). CASS registration: sort code and account number must be registered with Pay.UK CASS within 2 business days of account opening to enable incoming CASS switch payments to be routed correctly.
regulatory_sla.fscs_scv_sla: SCV updated within the provisioning transaction — synchronous requirement, not batch
regulatory_sla.cass_registration_sla: Sort code/account number registered with Pay.UK CASS within 2 business days of account opening
regulatory_sla.card_delivery_sla: Debit card delivered within 3–5 working days of account opening (bank policy; Visa/Mastercard scheme rules require personalised card production within specified timeframes)
references: PRA SS1/21 (Important Business Service impact tolerance)

latency.notes: Credential creation (SVC-100 write) is a sub-second operation. Biometric enrolment involves device-side FIDO2 processing (cryptographic key generation in secure enclave) plus an SVC-100 device registration write — total p95 target of 4,000ms. Push notification preferences update (SVC-053 write) is asynchronous and does not block activation confirmation. First-login SCA authentication is an incremental latency of ~1,000ms additional to biometric resolution.

throughput.burst_handling: SVC-100 (Identity & Access Management) must handle concurrent enrolment writes at peak throughput. Device registration writes are idempotent — duplicate enrolment attempts return the existing registration without creating duplicates.
throughput.notes: Biometric enrolment is device-local processing; server-side load for FIDO2 is the assertion verification at SVC-100, not the biometric computation.

availability.degraded_mode: If biometric enrolment fails, TOTP app fallback is offered automatically. If SVC-100 credential creation fails, activation is deferred with customer notification and a retry link emailed. Customers can transact via branch (CH-004) while digital channel activation is pending. Mobile app is designated as an Important Business Service under FCA PS21/3 — target availability must be maintained.
availability.ibs_note: Digital banking (mobile and web) is an Important Business Service under FCA PS21/3. FCA operational resilience requirements apply.

nfr.security_notes: Credential creation and biometric enrolment is the highest-security operation in the customer-facing phases. All credential writes use bcrypt (minimum cost factor 12) or Argon2id for password hashing. FIDO2 biometric templates remain on-device (iOS Secure Enclave / Android Strongbox) — the bank never receives raw biometric data, only the cryptographic WebAuthn assertion. Device registration must be logged to SVC-103 with device fingerprint. SCA enrolment must comply with PSR 2017 Regulation 100 and FCA RTS on SCA. New device registration triggers a security notification to the customer (fraud protection).

data_classification.sensitivity: HIGH — credential data is high-value attack target. Biometric enrolment status flag is personal data under UK GDPR (biometric processing under Article 9 requires explicit consent and DPIA).
data_classification.retention: Credential records retained for duration of customer relationship. Device registrations retained for 7 years post-deregistration for fraud investigation purposes.
data_classification.data_residency: UK only. SVC-100 must be hosted in UK-domiciled infrastructure.

regulatory_sla.obligation: SCA enrolment must be completed before the customer can authenticate into digital channels per PSR 2017 Regulation 100. The bank must not allow digital channel access without SCA-compliant authentication from the point of enrolment. Biometric data processing must be supported by explicit customer consent (UK GDPR Article 9(2)(a)) — consent must be obtained and recorded before enrolment.
regulatory_sla.sca_compliance: SCA must be applied to all online account access from first login; PSR 2017 Regulation 100 non-negotiable
references: UK GDPR Article 9 (biometric data — special category)

latency.notes: Welcome dashboard render on first authenticated session is a read from SVC-001 and SVC-017 — sub-second at p50. Welcome email dispatch (SVC-053 → email provider) must complete within 15 minutes of DigitalChannelActivated event. In-app welcome message is displayed synchronously on first login — it must not delay dashboard render. Cross-sell card rendering is non-blocking; loaded asynchronously from SVC-017.

throughput.burst_handling: Welcome email dispatch uses async event-driven processing (SVC-053 consuming WelcomePackDispatched events). Email provider (AWS SES / Twilio SendGrid) must have sufficient capacity for 800 emails/hour at peak. In-app notifications use SVC-053 push notification service — same capacity constraint applies.
throughput.notes: CASS switch prompt rendering requires a Pay.UK CASS eligibility check — this is asynchronous and must not block dashboard load.

availability.degraded_mode: If SVC-053 (notification service) is unavailable, welcome emails are queued for up to 2 hours and dispatched on recovery. Welcome dashboard render degrades gracefully if cross-sell cards cannot load — account balance and account details remain the primary required content. FSCS information sheet must be delivered — if in-app delivery fails, fallback to email delivery.
availability.notes: Availability target is marginally lower than provisioning (99.9% vs 99.95%) because welcome communications are not on the account opening critical path — the account is already open and operable.

nfr.security_notes: Welcome dashboard is a standard authenticated session — SCA enforced at login per PH-006 setup. Cross-sell product data is non-sensitive product information. CASS account numbers in the switch prompt are customer-provided PII — must be handled with standard PII controls. Push notification tokens (SVC-053) must not contain account number or balance data in the notification payload — balance data is fetched in-app only after authentication.

data_classification.sensitivity: MEDIUM — welcome communications contain account details (HIGH sensitivity in transit) but dashboard rendering uses already-authenticated session data. Vulnerability indicator flags are sensitive personal data under UK GDPR and FCA FG21/1 — access-controlled to authorised staff only.
data_classification.retention: Onboarding completion records retained for 5 years (Consumer Duty evidence). Vulnerability indicator flags retained for duration of customer relationship, reviewed annually. Marketing preferences retained until withdrawn (UK GDPR Article 7 — consent withdrawal).

regulatory_sla.obligation: FSCS information sheet and exclusions list must be provided at account opening (GOV-001-R02 — PRA Depositor Protection rules). This is a mandatory disclosure, not optional. Welcome pack dispatch must include the FSCS information sheet — failure to provide at account opening is a regulatory breach. CASS switch completion (if initiated at this phase): 7 working days from Switch Date (CASS guarantee — bank is contractually obligated to Pay.UK).
regulatory_sla.fscs_disclosure_sla: FSCS information sheet delivered within the welcome pack — within 15 minutes of account opening
regulatory_sla.cass_switch_sla: Current Account Switch Service (CASS) switch must complete within 7 working days of the customer-confirmed Switch Date. This is a Pay.UK guarantee scheme obligation, not a bank policy target. Failure to complete within 7 working days triggers the CASS guarantee compensation to the customer.
references: GOV-001-R02 (FSCS Depositor Protection — information disclosure at account opening)
CASS rules — Pay.UK (7 working day switch guarantee)
FCA PS22/9 Consumer Duty (consumer understanding — welcome communications clarity)
FCA FG21/1 (vulnerable customer identification — wellbeing questions)

end_to_end_journey_sla.description: The automated happy path (PH-001 through PH-007, no manual referral) should complete end-to-end within 10 minutes for a customer with a good network connection on the mobile app. This includes all system latencies across all phases. Neobank competitive benchmark: Monzo and Starling advertise sub-5-minute account opening for straightforward applications. The 10-minute target is conservative to accommodate biometric processing time and is a measurable operational KPI.

manual_referral_sla.description: Applications entering the AP-001 manual referral path must receive a final decision within 3 business days. This is a bank policy commitment disclosed to customers at referral. EDD for PEP cases must receive MLRO sign-off within this window.

audit_and_logging.all_phases: Every phase transition, participant action, system event, and domain event must be logged to SVC-103 (Audit & Logging). Events involving account creation, KYC decisions, and sanctions screening must additionally be written to SVC-111 (WORM/immutable store).

resilience_and_recovery.description: Recovery Point Objective (RPO): maximum 5 minutes of transactional data loss. Recovery Time Objective (RTO): account opening service restored within 30 minutes of a P1 incident. These targets are set relative to the Important Business Service impact tolerance under PRA SS1/21. The bank must test recovery capabilities at least annually.
references: PRA SS1/21 (Operational Resilience — Important Business Services)

data_protection_by_design.description: All phases must implement UK GDPR data minimisation (Article 5(1)(c)) — only personal data strictly necessary for the account opening purpose may be collected. Automated profiling of customers during the journey (risk scoring, eligibility decisioning) constitutes automated decision-making under UK GDPR Article 22 — customers must be informed of this and have the right to request human review of automated decisions. A DPIA must be maintained for the full JRN-001 journey and reviewed annually.
references: ICO guidance on automated decision-making in financial services

pci_dss.applicability: PCI DSS v4.0 applies from PH-005 onwards where card issuance is triggered. Card data (PAN, CVV2) is never stored by the bank — card production is handled by the card processor (Marqeta/Thredd) under their own PCI DSS compliance. The bank's scope is limited to the CardIssuanceTriggered event payload (which must not contain card data). In-app card detail display (PH-007) uses tokenised card references, not raw PANs.
